newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close sharply up on c.bank move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close sharply up on c.bank move.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply higher on Wednesday due to the central bank's persistent mop-up measures to tighten banking system's liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 7.437 percent against Tuesday's 6.977 percent close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was at 7.50 against 6.75 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers saw a firming trend for Thursday.
The central bank on Wednesday issued T$5 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit at an average yield of 7.513 percent.
The issue coincides with a long bull run in Taiwan's stock market, where the index has pushed to a series of seven-year highs in recent weeks.
The issue of T$11.85 billion in treasury bills, which were auctioned off on Tuesday, also tightened liquidity.
Taiwan stocks, which soared to an intraday high 9,648.43, lost momentum in the final hour of trade to close a scant 11.42 points or 0.12 percent lower at 9,544.56 on Wednesday.
Turnover remained a hectic T$258.8 billion, second only to Tuesday's all-time high of T$262 billion.
The huge turnover renewed concern in the market that the big stock market rally, which has doubled the index since March 1996, would be seen as driven by overly loose liquidity.

Analysts say the central bank's repeated issuance of NCDs in recent weeks has been aimed mainly at cooling the stock rally, though the central bank has called its actions a more general response to fine-tune money supply.
In the bond market, the benchmark 86/4 government bond yields rose slightly in early trade amid weak sentiment.
